question: Since NFA-A retained less capacity than the NCA reference after 100 cycles, by how many percentage points did it fall behind?

trace.query: SELECT id, kind, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE (page IN (10,11) AND (text ILIKE '%retention%' OR text ILIKE '%NCA%' OR text ILIKE '%NFA-A%' OR text ILIKE '%100 cycles%')) OR id LIKE 'p11.F8%' ORDER BY id
SELECT (CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM lines WHERE id='p11.L21'), '≈(\d+)%', 1) AS INT) - CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM lines WHERE id='p11.L22'), '≈(\d+)%', 1) AS INT)) AS gap

runs.text: Contrary to the premise, NFA-A did not fall behind the NCA reference. It retained more capacity over the cycle test:

runs.sql: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN id='p11.L21' THEN CAST(regexp_extract(text, '≈(\d+)%', 1) AS INT) END) - MAX(CASE WHEN id='p11.L22' THEN CAST(regexp_extract(text, '≈(\d+)%', 1) AS INT) END) AS gap FROM lines WHERE id IN ('p11.L21','p11.L22')

runs.text: percentage points at the end of the test. This matches the capacity retention figure, where the NFA A curve ends above the NCA curve.

rendered: Contrary to the premise, NFA-A did not fall behind the NCA reference. It retained more capacity over the cycle test: ≈80%[1] versus ≈68%[2], so NFA-A was ahead by 12[3] percentage points at the end of the test. This matches the capacity retention figure, where the NFA A curve ends above the NCA curve. Fig. 8[4]
